extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent owners and their attorneys/agents handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from the MPEP on handling citation of prior art and ex parte reexamination of patents, including requirements for priority/benefit claims, Office action content, and handling of special issues (Portola Packaging, res judicata, dependent claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-language prior art translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Portola Packaging may not prohibit reexamination over a complete and accurate translation of that foreign language prior art reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reexamination request explains why a more complete and accurate translation of the same foreign language prior art reference teaches what is required by the patent claims, it may be appropriate to rely on that foreign language prior art reference to order and/or conduct reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative (repetitive) references
rubrics_metrics.description: A cumulative reference that is repetitive is one that substantially reiterates verbatim the teachings of a reference that was either previously relied upon or discussed in a prior Office proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portola Packaging may prohibit reexamination based only on a repetitive reference. However, such a repetitive reference that cannot be considered will be rare because most references teach additional information or present information differently even when addressing the same subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice when prosecution terminated under Portola Packaging (NIRC wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution of an ongoing reexamination is terminated to comply with the Federal Circuit’s decision in In re Portola Packaging, the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate should state that the reexamination is terminated based on In re Portola Packaging and that no patentability determination has been made in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified language referencing In re Portola Packaging, Inc., 110 F.3d 786, 42 USPQ2d 1295 (Fed. Cir. 1997) and include explicit statement that no patentability determination has been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action wording when rejection withdrawn under Portola Packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rejection in the reexamination has previously been issued and that rejection is withdrawn to comply with In re Portola Packaging, the Office action withdrawing such rejection should state the withdrawal and that no patentability determination of the claims has been made in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the template phrasing: 'The rejection(s) based upon _______ is/are withdrawn in view of In re Portola Packaging, Inc., 110 F.3d 786, 42 USPQ2d 1295 (Fed. Cir. 1997). No patentability determination of the claims of the patent in view of such prior art has been made in this reexamination proceeding.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to correct foreign priority or domestic benefit during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may correct the failure to adequately claim foreign priority or domestic benefit in a patent to be reexamined during the reexamination proceeding in accordance with the section's guidelines; renewal of previously made claims of priority/benefit is not necessary during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications cannot claim the benefit of a provisional application. Specific petitions, fees, and supporting documents may be required depending on the filing dates and circumstances (see the detailed rules below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfecting foreign priority when claim was made before patent granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim for priority had been made before the patent was granted, submission of the certified copy in the reexamination proceeding is sufficient to perfect the foreign priority right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition to accept a delayed certified copy under 37 CFR 1.53(f)(3) is required (e.g., for applications that matured into the patent filed on or after March 16, 2013), a grantable petition, appropriate fee, and attachments must be filed in the file of the application that matured into the patent; a separate letter must be filed in the reexamination proceeding notifying the Office that the petition is being concurrently filed in the application file. Decisions on the petition will be placed in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting for first time both foreign priority claim and certified copy — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may obtain the right of foreign priority where it is necessary to submit for the first time both the claim for priority and the certified copy, but certain petitions may be required depending on the filing date of the application which matured into the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When required, a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e) must be filed in the application that matured into the patent; a separate letter must be filed in the reexamination proceeding identifying the concurrently filed petition and application number. Decisions and supporting ADS or other materials will be placed in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when the patent matured from an application filed on or after September 16, 2012 (foreign priority restoration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent matured from an application filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, the patent owner must file in the file of the application which matured into the patent: (a) a grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55(e); (b) an application data sheet identifying the foreign application (37 CFR 1.76(b)(6)) unless previously submitted; (c) a certified copy of the foreign application unless previously submitted or an exception applies; (d) the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(m)); and (e) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the reexamination proceeding, file a separate letter notifying the Office that items (a)-(e) are concurrently being filed in the application file. When a decision on the petition is rendered, a copy of the decision and any ADS determined to meet requirements will be placed in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when the patent matured from an application filed before September 16, 2012 (foreign priority restoration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent matured from an application filed before Sept 16, 2012, the grantable petition and required attachments must be filed in the application file specified by 37 CFR 1.55(c); a letter must be filed in the reexamination proceeding notifying the Office that the petition and attachments are concurrently being filed in that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on such petitions and any application data sheet, oath, or declaration determined to meet requirements will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP cross-references for further guidance on grantable petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoring right of foreign priority where subsequent filing was delayed (37 CFR 1.55(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition to restore the right of foreign priority and any required attachments must be filed in the application specified in 37 CFR 1.55(c), not in the reexamination proceeding, with a letter in the reexamination file notifying the Office of the concurrent filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a decision on the petition is rendered in the specified application's file, a copy of the decision and any ADS determined to meet requirements will be placed in the reexamination proceeding file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming domestic benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 — general correction during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may correct failure to adequately claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 of an earlier filed copending U.S. patent application during reexamination; for patents which matured from applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, a grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 37 CFR 1.78(e) must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition and attachments (except certain specification amendments) must be filed in the file of the application which matured into the patent, and a letter must be filed in the reexamination proceeding notifying the Office of the concurrent filing. Decisions and ADS placed in reexamination file when petition decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent matured from an application filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, the patent owner must file in that application's file: (a) a grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 37 CFR 1.78(e); (b) an application data sheet including the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2) unless previously submitted; (c) the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(m)); and (d) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the reexamination, file a letter notifying the Office that items (a)-(d) are concurrently being filed in the application file. When a decision on the petition is rendered, a copy will be placed in the reexamination file, and if granted, the ADS determined to meet requirements will be placed in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 for applications filed before September 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent matured from an application filed before Sept 16, 2012, the patent owner must file in the application file: (a) a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(e); (b) unless an amendment in the reexamination is chosen, an ADS including the required reference to the prior-filed application (37 CFR 1.76(b)(5)); (c) the petition fee; and (d) a statement that the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, the patent owner may file, in the reexamination proceeding, an amendment inserting the required reference into the specification first sentence(s) following the title as set forth in 37 CFR 1.78(h). A notifying letter must be filed in the reexamination. Decisions and ADS placed in reexamination file when petition decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) (provisional benefit) — requirements by filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may correct failure to adequately claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) of an earlier-filed provisional application, subject to filing a grantable petition when required; design applications cannot claim provisional benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents matured from applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, required items include a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(c), an ADS identifying the provisional (37 CFR 1.78(a)(3)) unless previously submitted, petition fee, and a statement the delay was unintentional; similar but slightly different options apply for patents from applications filed before Sept 16, 2012 (ADS vs amendment in reexamination). File notifying letter in reexamination and copies of decisions/ADS will be placed in reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoring benefit of a provisional application where filing of the subsequent application was delayed (37 CFR 1.78(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition to restore the benefit of a provisional application under 37 CFR 1.78(b), with required attachments including an ADS meeting 1.78(b), must be filed in the file of the application which matured into the patent (the subsequent application); a letter must be filed in the reexamination proceeding notifying the Office of the concurrent filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a decision on the petition is rendered in the subsequent application file, a copy of the decision and any ADS determined to meet requirements will be placed in the reexamination proceeding file. Design applications cannot claim provisional benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata and collateral estoppel do not bar reexamination in ordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims finally held valid by a federal court after all appeals will be withdrawn from consideration and not reexamined during reexamination proceedings. However, res judicata (claim preclusion) is not generally appropriate in reexamination because the Office was not a party to the litigation; issue preclusion (collateral estoppel) likewise cannot be applied against the Office where it lacked a 'full and fair opportunity' to litigate the issue (In re Trans Texas Holdings Corp.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP § 2242 and § 2286 for related Office policy when there has been a federal court decision on the merits. Court holdings in infringement proceedings do not automatically preclude reexamination by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and content expectations of the examiner's first Office action in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s first ex parte action on the merits should be the primary action to establish the issues between the examiner and the patent owner and should be sufficiently detailed to enable the second action to be properly made a final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First action should caution the patent owner to make a complete response because the next action is expected to be final; caution that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after final action; include a detailed statement of the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to each claim; if claim charts were submitted, the examiner may incorporate them but must carefully review them; the first action should respond to substance of arguments raised under 37 CFR 1.510, 1.530, and 1.535 and treat inappropriate arguments per 37 CFR 1.552(c). If relying on a patent owner statement under 1.501(a)(2), the requester must explain how that statement is being used to determine claim meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers to be submitted in response to the Office action (¶22.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure full consideration of any amendments, affidavits or declarations, or other documents as evidence of patentability, such documents must be submitted in response to this Office action. Submissions after the next Office action (intended to be final) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116 after final rejection and 37 CFR 41.33 after appeal, which will be strictly enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.04 in the first Office action to notify the patent owner of this requirement and the stricter rules for post-final submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of dependent claims in reexamination (2260.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unamended base patent claim has been rejected, canceled, or is no longer subject to reexamination due to adjudication in court, any claim undergoing reexamination which is directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be confirmed or allowed if the dependent claim is otherwise allowable and should not be objected to or rejected merely because it depends on a rejected or canceled patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No requirement should be made to rewrite the dependent claim in independent form. If a new base claim (other than original patent base claim) has been canceled in reexamination, a claim which depends thereon should be rejected as indefinite. If a new base claim or amended patent claim is rejected, a dependent claim should be objected to if it is otherwise patentable and a requirement made for rewriting the dependent claim in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status and priority (special dispatch) for reexamination proceedings (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination proceedings (including appeals to PTAB) will be conducted with special dispatch; reexamination proceedings involved in litigation will have priority over all other cases; reexaminations not involved in litigation will have priority over all other cases except those involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination proceedings are to be 'special' throughout their pendency. Prioritization rules must be applied accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content specifics for Office actions (2262)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s first Office action should state the examiner’s position and be so complete that the second Office action can properly be final. The first Office action must be sufficiently detailed to set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to the claims; claim charts may be incorporated but must be reviewed; subsequent actions must address patent owner responses to previous actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner concludes claims are patentable over cited prior art, indicate why similar to allowance (MPEP § 1302.14) and refer to record portions that clearly establish patentability. Normally, title changes are unnecessary; if needed, notify patent owner early. Examiner may indicate a telephone conference with patent owner’s representative may result in placing the proceeding in condition for NIRC; when conferences occur, actions must be properly signed/initialed by conferees per policy (see MPEP § 2271.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process of preparing the Office action (panel review conference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a patent owner response or expiration of response time, the examiner will prepare and set up a panel review conference as per MPEP § 2271.01 to discuss issuance of the Office action; the examiner may prepare the Office action before the conference and revise it after, or prepare it after the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel review (including conferees) and proper documentation (signatures/initials) are required when a conference confirms the examiner's preliminary decision to reject and/or allow claims.
